label: prop:coxeter-geometric-representation
title: The geometric representation: simple-injectivity at every Coxeter system
html:
Let M be a Coxeter matrix over an index set B. On the free module \bigoplus_{i \in B} \mathbb{R}\,\alpha_i equip the pairing with matrix entries \langle \alpha_i, \alpha_j \rangle = -\cos(\pi/m_{ij}) for i \neq j and \langle \alpha_i, \alpha_i \rangle = 1, and set

f_i \;=\; \mathrm{id} \;-\; 2\,\langle \alpha_i, \cdot\, \rangle\,
\alpha_i .

Then the f_i satisfy the Coxeter relations of M — (f_i f_j)^{m_{ij}} = 1 for every pair, at every bond order — so they assemble into the geometric representation of any Coxeter system (W, S) over M. Since f_i and f_j act with opposite signs on \alpha_i when i \neq j, the simple reflections of every Coxeter system are pairwise distinct: s_i \neq s_j with no hypothesis.

The bond-order relation at m_{ij} \geq 3 is a Chebyshev argument. Writing g = f_i f_j and tracking the scalar pair \bigl(\langle \alpha_i, g^k w \rangle, \langle \alpha_j, g^k w \rangle\bigr) of an arbitrary vector w, both components satisfy the second-order recursion

u_{k+2} \;=\; 2\cos\varphi \cdot u_{k+1} \;-\; u_k,
\qquad \varphi = \tfrac{2\pi}{m_{ij}},

whose solutions are trigonometric and hence m_{ij}-periodic. The action of g^k differs from the identity by singles accumulated from these scalars; periodicity and telescoping force both accumulated sums to vanish, the coefficient matrix being invertible because \cos^2(\pi/m_{ij}) < 1. Thus g^{m_{ij}} w = w. The remaining orders are elementary: m_{ij} = 2 is direct commutation of the two reflections, and the diagonal is the involution f_i^2 = 1.

Combined with the collapsed Tits residue, every hypothesis in the parabolic-transversal chain is discharged: the braid and far-commutation relations on the length-rule module hold for every Coxeter system unconditionally.
